confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on 2026 aggregated cost-of-living data found by web search. For an inexpensive meal, Numbeo data reported via Expatica gives about $25, MyLifeElsewhere gives $25-33 and Expat Arrivals gives no figure; I used $25. A mid-range meal for two is about $100-105 across sources. A cappuccino is about $4.92-5.55. A domestic draft beer is about $6-7.50. Cocktail figures range from $11-12 in Square menu-pricing data to $14-17 in a Cities Insider guide citing Expatistan and Livingcost, and Expatistan's own $17 estimate rests on few data points; I used about $14. No aggregated restaurant price for a glass of wine was found; the only figure was a retail bottle price of about $19 from Expatistan. The wine anchor is therefore estimated from its usual US relationship to beer and cocktail prices, at about 1.8x beer and a little below a cocktail, and is low-confidence. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not checked against live listings. Atlanta has very few registered hostels, so the dorm and private hostel figures are the most uncertain. July 2026 hotel rates are adjusted upward for summer demand and FIFA World Cup 2026 matches at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, which could push actual event-date prices well above these figures. Prices vary a lot by neighbourhood: Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead cost more than outlying areas.
comparable_city_reasoning: Atlanta is a large US Sun Belt city whose restaurant prices are near or slightly above the national average. Comparable cities include Charlotte, Nashville, Dallas and Houston, and its prices are well below New York, Boston and San Francisco. Accommodation reasoning uses typical US big-city budget motel and three-star chain hotel pricing, with a summer and event-demand adjustment for July 2026.
